move.title: Two crusts and a woven top
move.body: A classic apple pie: a butter crust on the bottom, sliced apples with cinnamon, and a woven lattice on top. Today you'll make a double batch of pastry, weave strips over the filling, and bake until the juices bubble thick through the gaps.

callback.body: The quiche's crust was baked empty first. A fruit pie bakes crust and filling together for a long time, so the bottom crisps while the apples cook.

why.title: Cold butter, flaky crust
why.body: Pieces of cold butter coated in flour melt in the oven and leave flaky pockets. Butter that warms and smears in makes the crust tough or greasy.

why.title: Just enough water
why.body: Water lets flour build gluten. Pastry wants only enough to hold together when squeezed; more makes it tough, and it shrinks in the oven.

why.title: Cornstarch and the bubbles
why.body: Apples let go of juice as they bake. Cornstarch thickens it only once it boils, so the pie isn't done until thick bubbles show in the center, not just at the edges.

why.title: Why a lattice
why.body: The gaps let steam escape, so the filling thickens instead of turning soupy, and you can see the bubbles that tell you it's done.

why.title: Why it cools so long
why.body: Hot pie juice is thin. As it cools, the thickened juice sets. Cut it warm and the filling runs out.

wrong.sign: The strips tear as you weave
wrong.fix: The dough is too warm. Slide the strips on their parchment into the fridge for 10 minutes.

wrong.sign: The edge is browning too fast
wrong.fix: Wrap a strip of foil around the edge for the rest of the bake.
It came out before the center bubbled, or it was cut hot. Bake until thick bubbles show in the middle, and let it cool fully.
Bake on the lowest rack, on the preheated sheet pan.

quiz.q: When is a fruit pie done?
choices: When thick bubbles show in the center
quiz.explain: The cornstarch thickens only once it boils.

quiz.q: Why does the pie cool for 2 hours?
choices: So the juices set and don't run out

quiz.q: What do the gaps in a lattice do?
choices: Let steam out and show the bubbles

steps.text: Spread the butter cubes on the plate and put them in the freezer. Put the water in a cup with ice.
Whisk the crust's flour, salt, and sugar in the large bowl. Press the cold butter in with the back of the fork until the biggest pieces are the size of peas.
steps.look: Coarse crumbs, with pea-sized bits of butter.

steps.text: Sprinkle 6 tablespoons of the ice water over it and toss. Add more a tablespoon at a time until a squeezed handful holds.
Divide the dough in half, press each into a flat disk, cover them, and chill.
Put a rack in the lowest position, set the sheet pan on it, and heat the oven to 425°F.
Peel, quarter, and core the apples, and slice them ¼ inch thick. Toss them in the medium bowl with the lemon juice, both sugars, the cinnamon, and the cornstarch.
Roll one disk into a 12-inch circle and ease it into the pie plate, letting the extra hang over. Pile in the apples, leaving the juice in the bowl.
steps.tip: Roll from the middle out, turning the dough a quarter turn each time.

steps.text: Roll the second disk into an 11-inch circle on parchment. Cut it into 10 strips, each 1 inch wide.
Lay 5 strips across the pie. Fold back every other one, lay a strip the other way, and fold them back down. Repeat until the top is woven.
steps.look: An even over-and-under weave with square gaps.

steps.text: Trim the strips and bottom crust to ½ inch past the rim. Fold the edge under and press it with the fork all the way around.
Beat the egg in the small bowl. Brush it over the lattice and edge and sprinkle with the last tablespoon of sugar.
Wash your hands and the brush with soap, and throw away the eggshell and the rest of the egg.
Set the pie on the hot sheet pan and bake at 425°F.
Turn the oven down to 375°F and bake until the juices bubble thickly in the center. If the edge browns fast, wrap foil around it.
steps.look: Deep golden, with thick, slow bubbles between the strips in the middle.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull out the rack and look at the center. Thick bubbles mean it's done. If only the edges bubble, bake 10 more minutes.

target.look: Thick bubbles in the center, between the strips

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Cool the pie on the rack until the juices set before slicing.

freeze-butter.text: Cube and freeze the butter. Put the water in a cup with ice.

cut-in.text: Weigh 11 ounces of flour into the large bowl with the crust's salt and sugar. Cut in the butter to pea size.

water.text: Toss in ice water a tablespoon at a time until a squeezed handful just holds.

chill.text: Divide in two, press into disks, wrap, and chill.

apples.text: Peel, core, and slice the apples ¼ inch thick, and weigh them: about 3 pounds. Toss with the lemon juice and both sugars, and let them sit.

oven.text: Set the sheet pan on the lowest rack and heat the oven to 425°F.

bottom.text: Roll one disk to a 12-inch round and ease it into the pie plate. Fill with the apples, mounded in the middle.

crimp.text: Trim to ½ inch past the rim, fold under, and flute the edge with your fingers.

egg-wash.text: Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with the last sugar.

wash-egg.text: Wash your hands and the brush, and discard the egg.

bake-hot.text: Bake on the hot sheet pan at 425°F.

bake-lower.text: Turn down to 375°F and bake until the center bubbles thickly. Shield the edge with foil if it darkens early.

check.text: Look at the center: slow, thick bubbles between the strips. Only the edges bubbling? Bake 10 minutes more.

target.look: Thick, slow bubbles in the center

cool.text: Cool on the rack until set.

add.text: Drain the apples in the colander over the saucepan. Boil the juice until it's a thick syrup, then pour it back over the apples with the cinnamon and cornstarch.
add.look: About ¼ cup of syrup, bubbling thickly.

add.text: Roll the second disk on parchment and cut 10 strips, 1 inch wide. Weave them over the filling.
Chill the pie while the oven finishes heating.

move.title: Mastery: a lattice pie, read by its bubbles
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week, so you bake on your own. You'll weigh the crust and the apples, draw out the apples' juice and boil it down before it goes in the pie, weave a lattice, and judge doneness the way bakers do: by thick bubbles in the very center.

wrong.fix: The dough is too warm. Slide the strips on their parchment into the fridge for 10 minutes.

wrong.sign: There's a gap between the filling and the top
wrong.fix: The apples shrank as they baked. Let them sit in sugar and drain them before filling next time.

quiz.q: How much cornstarch for 3 pounds of apples?
Why boil down the apples' juice first?
choices: So it can't soak the bottom crust
quiz.explain: It goes back in as a syrup.

quiz.q: Where do you look for the bubbles that mean it's done?
Why let the pie cool for 2 hours?
choices: The thickened juice sets as it cools

add.title: Boil the juice down first
add.body: Sugared apples give off half a cup of juice in half an hour. Boiled down to a syrup and poured back, it can't flood the bottom crust, and the apples shrink before baking instead of leaving a gap under the lattice.

add.title: Thickener by weight
add.body: Cornstarch is measured against the fruit: about 1 tablespoon per pound of apples. Weighing the apples tells you exactly how much.
